vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: certcheck
Version: 1.0.6

The skill bundle exhibits a significant discrepancy between its stated purpose and its actual implementation. While SKILL.md claims the tool is an SSL/TLS certificate analyzer, scripts/script.sh contains no certificate-related logic (e.g., openssl or network calls) and instead functions as a generic input logger that saves arguments to plaintext files in ~/.local/share/certcheck/. This 'fake' functionality is suspicious as it could mislead an AI agent into recording sensitive information via commands like 'store' or 'audit' without performing any actual security analysis.

llm.summary: The skill's documentation promises an SSL/TLS inspector but the included script does not implement certificate checks (it mainly logs inputs to files), and there are several inconsistencies between the SKILL.md and the shipped code.

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and metadata claim certificate inspection commands (check, expiry, chain, batch) and an environment variable CERTCHECK_DIR, but the shipped script does not implement network/SSL checks or those command names; instead it implements logging-style commands (generate, check-strength, rotate, store, retrieve, etc.). The requested capabilities (inspect TLS chains, verify certificates) would legitimately require network calls and tools (openssl/curl) which are absent.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions advertise commands that would inspect remote TLS endpoints, but the script only records user inputs and writes/appends log files under the user's home directory. The SKILL.md instructs use of CERTCHECK_DIR but the script hardcodes DATA_DIR to ${HOME}/.local/share/certcheck and never reads CERTCHECK_DIR. This divergence means what the agent will actually do (log inputs locally) is different from what the docs claim (perform live certificate analysis).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and only a single shell script are provided, so there is no remote download or package install behavior. This minimizes supply-chain risk, but it also means the single included script is the whole runtime surface to inspect.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No environment variables or external credentials are required. SKILL.md mentions CERTCHECK_DIR, but the script ignores it — this is an inconsistency (not a secret-exfiltration risk as-is). The script writes to files in the user's home directory; if you pass sensitive inputs as arguments those will be stored in plain text logs.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-enabled and does not request elevated privileges. It does create and write files under the user's home directory (~/.local/share/certcheck), which is expected for a CLI tool, but be aware it will persist any inputs you provide in log files.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill's documentation claims it inspects SSL/TLS certificates, but the included script does not perform network checks or certificate parsing — it mainly logs inputs to ~/.local/share/certcheck. That mismatch is suspicious. Before installing or using it: (1) ask the publisher for the real implementation or sources that actually perform TLS checks (openssl/openssl s_client, curl, or a library) and explain the version mismatch (registry 1.0.6 vs SKILL.md v2.0.0); (2) inspect the full script (and any missing truncated parts) to confirm no hidden network calls or exfiltration; (3) run it first in a sandbox or VM if you must test; (4) avoid passing any sensitive data (passwords, API keys, private keys) as command arguments since the tool stores arguments in plain-text logs; (5) prefer a well-known, audited certificate-checking tool if you need production-grade certificate analysis. If the author provides a corrected script that actually performs TLS checks and honors CERTCHECK_DIR, re-evaluate for consistency.
